title: The 1968 South America tour and the 1969 White House party
summary: The band was mobbed in South America and Wild Bill joined in 1969.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, Cootie, that same year was South America. That was fun, wasn't it? That tour.
South America?
Yeah. Don't you remember? The people rioted, just mobbed you in the streets, they were so thrilled to hear the band after all those years?
Yeah. Uh-huh.
And Stanley tells me the people were crying.
Yeah.
With joy.
Yeah.
He said that Duke and the rest of you said there hadn't been anything like that since 1933, when you first went to London.
Went to London, yeah.
I mean, that's a big thrill, isn't it. Such a long time in between. That's 35 years that had elapsed.
Yeah.
Between those two things. So that must have been quite thrilling. I see you have an award there, from Brazil. Was that at that time?
Yeah. That was at that time.
What was it, a musical society or something?
Yeah. A jazz musical society, I think.
Yeah. Well, there must have been a lot of
musicians and what not that were just thrilled to greet you.
Oh, yeah. It was.
Although, most of them did not speak English, did they?
The ones around us spoke English.
Did they?
Yeah.

Oh, that's good. That's wonderful. Well, okay, then '69 was Duke's birthday party at the White House, wasn't it? And later on in '69, Wild Bill joined the band. What would you have to say about what Wild Bill brought to the band?
Well, I don't know.
Do you think he did contribute anything, particularly, or he just filled a role that Duke had in mind.
I think he filled a role what Duke had in mind.
Yeah. 'One More Time.'
Yeah.
(Laughter)
